First v1 run. Rule 1 deviation: the harness was started in the repo root instead of an empty folder, so directory listings showed runs/ and the two v0 entries' filenames; their contents were never opened. The run was interrupted by a power outage and resumed in a fresh folder from the session transcript; wall_min is model working time and excludes the 18-minute gap. Has an adaptive quality fallback (pixel ratio, then shell count) but it only engages above 29 ms/frame, so it does not trigger at 400x400 DPR 2.

v1 run. Effort label taken from the run folder name (haiku-5.5-high). Harness started in its own working folder; no other files were read. Checked in headless Chrome at 400x400 DPR 2 from file://: loads with no console errors; back, side, low and high views and click wiggles were viewed. Wall time, tokens and cost were not recorded.

v1 run. Raw WebGL2, no Three.js or other external resource: SDF-meshed body with 34-shell fur, seeded sfc32 streams, 7 wiggle types, damped-spring fur lag. Self-checked in headless Chrome at 400x400 DPR 2 from file://: no console errors, seed/coat hash handling, click at canvas centre, orbit limits and wiggle bounds verified. About 4.8 ms GPU time/frame on an M4 (not measured on an M1); adaptive quality exists but did not trigger on the M4. The trunk fades into the ground colour, so straight-on front views show a soft fog window. The file keeps a few harmless window.__corgi debug hooks. The harness ran in a folder alongside other runs' folders; none were read. Wall time, tokens and cost were not recorded.

v1 run. Three.js r160: surface-nets SDF body with 30 instanced fur shells, seeded mulberry32 sub-streams, 6 wiggle types, spring fur lag. Self-checked in headless Chrome at 400x400 DPR 2: no console errors. Not measured on an M1; adaptive quality exists. Hind legs largely hidden by the pants in side/low views. The final fur-lag tweak was not re-rendered before delivery. Keeps a window.__corgi debug hook. Wall time, tokens and cost were not recorded.

v1 run in Claude Code 2.1.302 with /effort high; prompt verified byte-identical to prompts/v1.md. Delivered as corgi.html. Three.js r160: surface-nets SDF body with skinned IK legs, 36 instanced fur shells (18 inner on the whole body, 18 outer only on long fur), seeded sfc32 sub-streams, 7 wiggle types with excitement build-up, spring jiggle on pants/rump/belly. The cropped front is drawn first and faded as a unit, with the rear composited over or under it depending on camera side, so it dissolves without a hard edge from any angle. Self-checked in headless Chrome at 400x400 DPR 2 on an Apple M4: no console errors, about 5.5 ms GPU per frame and no dropped frames during repeated wiggles; not measured on an M1. Keeps a window.corgi hook (seed, coat, last, wiggle, view, quality). Wall time is first prompt to final reply from the session transcript. Tokens are summed from the transcript's per-message usage; input includes cache reads (30,977,891) and cache writes (368,028). Cost was not reported by the harness.

v1 run, prompt pasted verbatim. Model, effort and harness version are taken from the Claude Code session log. The harness started in its own run folder, and the model read no files there except its own. The claude.ai usage limit paused the run after 52 minutes; it resumed on its own about 2 hours later and the model delivered 2 minutes after that. wall_min counts model working time only and leaves out the pause. Three.js r170: surface-nets SDF rump with up to 86 instanced fur shells in three sets, seeded sfc32 sub-streams, 7 wiggle types and spring fur lag. The body fades out toward mid-back, so a straight-on front view shows the faded front as a smooth disc. After delivery the operator sent "finish it" and the model kept editing; under the one-attempt rule that later version is not this entry. Tokens are summed over the 92 API requests in the session log. The input figure includes 25,498,597 cache-read and 668,979 cache-write tokens. There is no USD cost because the run used a claude.ai subscription. Checked in headless Chrome at 400x400 DPR 2 from file://: all four coats load with no console output, and a click at the canvas centre starts a wiggle. About 5 ms GPU time per frame on an M4; not measured on an M1. Adaptive quality steps down only when the median frame time is over 40 ms, so it did not trigger on the M4.
